name: MI-13
label: Safe D

key_factors: Open seat with well-funded Democratic nominee McKinney
Republican nominee lacks fundraising or outside support
Prediction markets price Democratic win near 98%
model.rationale: The seat's +22 Democratic lean and an open-seat dynamic favor the party holding the district, and Donavan McKinney has raised $1.4 million with outside backing while the Republican nominee shows no measurable fundraising. Markets price a Democratic win near certainty, so the forecast stays safely Democratic with only a modest haircut for the open seat.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending for the Republican nominee or an unexpected scandal involving McKinney could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Shri Thanedar (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Detroit-area MI-13 is a heavily Democratic open seat after Shri Thanedar lost renomination to state Rep. Donavan McKinney, who enters the general with strong fundraising and outside support. The Republican nominee, T. P. Nykoriak, has no reported fundraising or outside spending, and minor-party and independent candidates are on the ballot but poorly funded.

The district's +22 Democratic partisan lean makes a Republican upset implausible, and prediction markets price a Democratic win near 98%. The main uncertainty is turnout and the size of the margin rather than the winner, so the race is rated Safe Democratic with wide but ordinary uncertainty.
